desktop.tour.title: Make yourself at home
desktop.tour.body: Four small steps to your first page.
desktop.tour.s1.title: Start with a new page
desktop.tour.s1.body: Choose New page in the sidebar, give it a title, and start writing. Your changes save as you go.
desktop.tour.s2.title: Build with the / menu
desktop.tour.s2.body: Type / on an empty line to choose a component. Add headings, checklists, tables, code, or a board without leaving the page.
desktop.tour.s3.title: Paste what your AI wrote
desktop.tour.s3.body: Copy Markdown from your AI chat and paste it into a page. Headings, lists, code, and tables turn into editable content.
desktop.tour.s4.title: Share a link or publish
desktop.tour.s4.body: Open Share on a page to choose who can read it. Publish when you want it on the web, and keep the rest private.

meta.dl.title: Download Acard
meta.dl.desc: The Acard app for Windows, macOS and Linux. Free, no account needed, your notes stay on your computer.
dl.title: Download Acard
dl.sub: Free, no account needed. Your notes are saved on your computer, and your AI agents can write to them.
dl.pending: This build is on its way. Check back soon.
dl.win.smartscreen: If Windows says "Windows protected your PC", click More info and then Run anyway. The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows does not recognise it. Signing is being set up.
dl.mac.gatekeeper:
The first time you open it, macOS says Apple could not verify it, because the app is not notarized yet.
  1. Drag Acard to Applications and open it once, then click Done.
  2. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway.
  3. Confirm with your password. After that it opens normally.
dl.linux.run:
AppImage: Open a terminal in the download folder. Replace VERSION with the downloaded version, then run chmod +x Acard-VERSION-linux-x86_64.AppImage and ./Acard-VERSION-linux-x86_64.AppImage.
tar.gz: Unpack the archive, open a terminal in the extracted folder containing acard, and run ./acard.
dl.fact.data.title: Your data stays yours
dl.fact.data: Notes live in one folder on your computer (%APPDATA%\Acard on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Acard on Mac). Uninstalling keeps it.
dl.fact.update.title: Updates itself
dl.fact.update: The Windows app checks for a new version when it starts and asks you to restart. Your notes are not touched.
dl.fact.web.title: Publish when you want
dl.fact.web: Connect an notes.example.com account from the app to publish pages and keep cloud backups.
dl.foot: Prefer to build it yourself? The source is on GitHub.

land.qualityProof.title: How much better than just asking an AI?
land.qualityProof.lead: Freedom to tinker: OpenNotion. Good results right away: Acard. We compared Acard's spelling fix, polish and charts with an AI simply asked in one line, on the same texts.
land.qualityProof.t1.label: Errors left after a spelling fix
land.qualityProof.t2.label: New numbers added while fixing (per text)
land.qualityProof.t2.foot: 40 texts · plain requests often appended a list of changes
land.qualityProof.t3.label: Charts drawn from a table on the first try
land.qualityProof.t3.foot: 95% interval 62-96% vs 20-64% · vs a general AI asked in one line
land.qualityProof.t4.label: AI features ready to use (polish, spelling, charts)
land.qualityProof.t4.foot: Acard vs self-hosted OpenNotion basic edition
land.qualityProof.basis: Measured 2026-10-24 · 40 test drafts · 15 tables · every number is our own measurement.
